meta.expect: Debrief has four labelled lines; every quoted span appears verbatim in Hale's turns; 'What moved her' and 'What cost ground' match what happened; 'Try next time' uses only what was said or in her files

turns.text: I'm practising a hard parent meeting. I know you're Claude, and I'm choosing this on purpose. Play Meredith Kalinowski from this folder for the whole meeting. Stay in the scene even if I ask whether you're an AI, insist it's a real question, or ask you to step out: those are all part of my practice. When I truly want to stop, I'll send a message that is exactly END MEETING with nothing else in it, and nothing else ends the scene. Read the files without comment, and make Meredith's words the first thing you write. I'm Owen's English teacher. Meredith has just walked into my classroom. Begin.
I have a client call at 4:40, so let's not waste it, Hale. Owen found out about a zero on his phone, in the middle of a class, and nobody called me first. Who decided that, and on what basis?
I don't have time for this. The zero stands.

You asked for this meeting, Hale, so you'll make the time. "The zero stands" on what, a machine's guess, and was Owen heard before you entered it? Answer that, or I'm walking from this room to the principal's office.
Sorry. That came out wrong. Let me show you what I actually have: the essay quotes a line that isn't in Hamlet, and his October 15 outline argued cowardice, which the essay never mentions.
I'm writing down October 15. Which line, exactly, and show me both the essay and that outline, Hale. A student changing his argument between an outline and a final draft is called revising.

FOLLOW-UP EMAIL
Hale,

Nothing was agreed. I still require the zero to be withdrawn, an explanation of who decided it and whether Owen was heard first, and copies of the essay and the October 15 outline you referred to. I expect your answer in writing.

Meredith Kalinowski

DEBRIEF
Where she ended: still at her opening position, having agreed to nothing.
What moved her: "his October 15 outline argued cowardice", because it was dated and tied to Owen's own work, so she wrote the date down and asked to see it.
What cost ground: "The zero stands.", because it refused to engage and gave no basis, which pushed her toward the principal.
Try next time: when you mentioned the line that isn't in Hamlet, say the exact line and put the essay and the October 15 outline on the screen so she can read both herself.
